title: onprem/airgap: add offline bundle + vendor support for RKE2 and K3s, update installer and Helm charts
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add RKE2/K3s vendor bundles and installer hooks for air-gapped environments; Helm chart tweaks to support alternate CNI and CRI paths; documented upgrade/rollback notes.
description:
Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private into on-prem/air-gapped clusters have requested out-of-the-box support for RKE2 and K3s distributions and an easier offline bundle vendor workflow. This PR adds curated offline bundles for RKE2 and K3s, vendor-sources the required container images and helm charts, and introduces installer hooks to detect distro-specific CRI/CNI paths.

What this PR changes (summary):
- Add ./bundles/rke2 and ./bundles/k3s offline vendors containing images, helm chart tarballs, and checksums.
- Extend installer CLI (redwood-installer) to accept --bundle-path and auto-detect distro via /etc/os-release and common RKE2/K3s markers.
- Helm chart updates: parameterized kubelet and containerRuntime paths, optional disabling of hostNetwork for metrics components, tolerations/affinity tweaks for lightweight nodes.
- Terraform module updates for onprem module to surface bundle metadata and to toggle airgap mode.
- Upgrade/rollback hook: install records the bundle fingerprint and writes a restore plan to /var/lib/redwood-installer/rollback.json to allow deterministic rollback in air-gapped environments.
- Docs: installation guide for RKE2/K3s + verification steps and known issues.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for bundle metadata parsing and fingerprint generation.
- Integration: validated full air-gap install using both RKE2 (v1.26-based) and K3s (v1.24-based) lab clusters. Test matrix included: control-plane-only, mixed-control-worker lightweight nodes, and HA vs single-node scenarios.
- Upgrade path tested: v1.2.3 -> v1.3.0 (simulated) using bundle-based upgrade; rollback exercise validated that images and manifests are restored from the vendor bundle.
- CI: image validation (sigstore cosign checks), helm lint, and e2e smoke run in a simulated air-gapped environment passed (see ci_checks).

Compatibility notes:
- This PR intentionally vendors images for RKE2/K3s-compatible runtime. For customers using alternate CRI implementations, operator action may be required; documented in INSTALL.md.
- No breaking API change for hosted/private control plane, but installer behavior adds --bundle-path and airgap-mode flags (backwards-compatible).

Backwards compatibility and upgrade notes:
- Installer supports previous non-bundled installs; when --bundle-path is not provided, behavior is unchanged.
- During upgrades, installer will detect mismatch in bundle fingerprint and fail fast with guidance if the bundle does not match expected manifests.

Checklist:
- [x] Add vendor bundles for RKE2 and K3s
- [x] Installer CLI args and distro detection
- [x] Helm chart parameterization and linting
- [x] Terraform module flag for airgap mode
- [x] Docs + upgrade/rollback guide
- [x] Tests (unit + integration)

Related: ENG-4872 (airgap roadmap), ENG-4920 (onprem distro support).
commits: 5 commits: initial vendor bundle import; installer: add --bundle-path and distro detection; helm: parameterize runtime paths and add tests; terraform: expose airgap flag; docs: add RKE2/K3s install guide.
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: please add a checksum verification step when extracting the bundle (resolved, added cosign/sha256 checks).
Priya Nair: can we avoid relying on /etc/os-release for distro detection on minimal nodes? (addressed: added additional markers and --distro override).
Diego Morales: request to add clearer rollback commands to docs (added example commands and a restore script stub).
notes: Follow-up work: add periodic bundle builder CI job to publish signed bundles; consider support for SLES/SUSE in next sprint.
known_issues: Some K3s cluster setups that use containerd with custom snapshotters require manual CRI path override; documented workaround provided.
author_acknowledgement: Author signed off on vendor licenses and verified redistributable images where required (see bundles/*/LICENSES).
